proof_check: (a) machine-checked in Lean (Infinity.C12.residue_grundy, Infinity.C12.power_of_two_grundy; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no sorry); (b) written proof (proofs/paper/C12.md Theorem 5); 0 mismatches for k = 2..20, n <= 2e4 (EXP-C12-02)
statement:
(a) If no element of the move set S is divisible by q and 1, ..., q - 1 are in S, the subtraction game S has
g(n) = n mod q; in particular subtract-a-power-of-2 has g(n) = n mod 3. (b) For every k >= 2,
subtract-a-power-of-k has the same Grundy function as the subtraction game {1, k}: n mod 2 for odd k, and
P(n mod (k + 1)) with P(r) = r mod 2 for r < k and P(k) = 2 for even k.
title: Residue lemma; subtract-a-power-of-k has the Grundy function of the subtraction game {1, k}
